18.5. Pennaiyar River

The river Pennaiyar is one of the 15 Rivers mentioned in Schedule-A

of the Madras-Mysore Agreement, 1892. As per Clause-II of the

agreement, the upstream State should not, without the previous

consent of the downstream Tamil Nadu State, build any new Anicut or

any structure to obstruct, divert or store the waters of the river across

any part of the river.

When the Government of Karnataka planned Check Dams and

diversion structures across the river Pennaiyar and Markandeyanadhi,

Tributary of Pennaiyar, in spite of the repeated requests from Tamil

Nadu against the above works of Karnataka, it went ahead with the

construction works. Hence, Tamil Nadu filed an Original Suit (O.S No.

1 of 2018) and an I.A on 18.5.2018 in the Hon’ble Supreme Court,

seeking intervention, restraining the State of Karnataka from

proceeding with the construction of Check Dam / Dam across

Markandeyanadhi, and other diversion structure across the Pennaiyar

river and its tributaries, and pumping water from them to the existing

tanks in the Pennaiyar basin in Karnataka.

The Hon’ble Supreme Court, in its Judgment dated 14.11.2019 in the

I.A.No.95384 of 2019 filed by Tamil Nadu on 3.7.2019, granted liberty

A scheme to provide water supply to more than one habitation or to cover all the habitations in a village panchayat, if the source is available within the VP is referred as Single Village Scheme.

The State Monitoring Officers for each district would also monitor the progress during the field visits

Involving Grama Sabha / Local bodies - All Projects implemented in the village panchayat would be presented in the Grama Sabha, approval by the Grama Sabha for selecting/ approving beneficiaries and selecting land or building for running other projects.

Evaluation of sanctioned projects / completed projects would be taken up from State Planning Commission both from within and through external agencies.

In the case of line departments the entire scheme is considered as one project. Hence, the monitoring and evaluation will be carried out by the State Level Empowered Committee based on the quarterly reports submitted by the departments. The State Planning Commission will be in touch with the Nodal officers designated for the projects in the respective Government departments implementing the project directly.

Concurrent Evaluation

Provision shall also be made for concurrent evaluation of the progress in attaining the output-outcome envisaged in the program. This evaluation can be entrusted to any reputed institution or agency and will not exceed 1% of the allotment totally. The decision on the evaluation team and cost will be decided by the State Level Empowered Committee. The State Level Empowered Committee can recommend and approve deviations. The modalities of concurrent evaluation will be decided in the State Level Empowered Committee.

(cont.)

-9- Maintenance of Accounts

Each implementing agency shall be responsible for maintenance of accounts for the funds received by them. The implementing agency entrusted with funds under the programme shall maintain separate account to enable audit.

Audit of works

Regular physical and financial audit of the works under the scheme shall be carried out by a charted accountant at the end of each financial year at the state level. The report issued by the auditor shall be presented to the State Level Empowered Committee and further sanction of funds would be considered only based on the proper financial management.

Inspection of Works

In order to maintain quality of works, a quality monitoring system shall be constituted. The Heads of division, Planning Officers of the State Planning Commission may tour the districts to inspect the works periodically / monthly basis and report progress to the Member Secretary / Vice Chairman. The system shall be reviewed regularly by the State Level Empowered Committee.

Interventions and Expected Outcomes

The project proposal/ action plans are prepared to address certain backwardness / issues. In order to track the deliverables, outputs with the expected outcomes, an output-outcome monitoring framework would be prepared. This would be followed and reviewed so that objectives are achieved as planned. The result will be placed before State Level Empowered Committee periodically once in 6 months.
